extracted.intended_audience: national and county government officials, Ministries/Departments/Agencies (MDAs), constitutional commissions, non-state actors (CSOs/NGOs/FBOs/CBOs), and other stakeholders involved in public participation in Kenya
extracted.subtask_description: A draft national policy establishing definitions, objectives, principles, standards and an implementation framework for public participation in Kenya, binding national and county public bodies and guiding non-state actors and citizens.

rubrics_metrics.name: Public Participation (definition)
rubrics_metrics.description: Public Participation: refers to the process by which citizens, as individuals, groups or communities (also known as stakeholders), take part in the conduct of public affairs, interact with the state and other non-state actors to influence decisions, policies, programs, legislation and provide oversight in service delivery, development and other matters concerning their governance and public interest, either directly or through freely chosen representatives.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Used as the working definition for the policy; implies inclusion of individuals, groups, communities, direct and representative participation, and a broad set of governance matters.

rubrics_metrics.name: Facilitation of Public Participation (definition)
rubrics_metrics.description: Facilitation of Public Participation: to facilitate means to 'make easy or easier' or to 'promote'; 'taking steps to ensure the public is involved or is brought into the matter'.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Implies active measures by duty-bearers to remove barriers and promote involvement rather than passive invitation only.

rubrics_metrics.name: Accountability (definition)
rubrics_metrics.description: Accountability: means answerability to the people: an open transparent system which permits the free flow of forward and backward information and in which leaders are answerable to the people.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Links public participation to transparent information flows and leaders' obligation to explain and justify decisions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Standards (definition)
rubrics_metrics.description: Standards: means the act or process of public participation is developed and accepted by the stakeholders as of the desired content and quality. The standards are based on the consensus of different interested parties, users, and by the two levels of government.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Sets expectation that participation processes should meet agreed content/quality thresholds and be the product of multi-stakeholder consensus.

rubrics_metrics.name: Coordination (definition)
rubrics_metrics.description: Coordination: refers to the ability or process of organizing different stakeholders to ensure that they work together in harmony, effectively and efficiently.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Framing public participation as a multi-actor activity requiring harmonization to avoid duplication and conflict.

rubrics_metrics.name: Objective: Ensure access to timely information in easy-to-understand language and format
rubrics_metrics.description: Ensure citizens continually access timely information on public issues in a language and format that is easy to understand;
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Requires information be timely, in accessible languages and formats (including accessible formats for PWDs), and presented in ways citizens can comprehend.

rubrics_metrics.name: Objective: Provide framework for coordination and enabling environment for NSAs
rubrics_metrics.description: Provide a framework for coordination and enabling environment for NSAs involved in civic education;
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Calls for institutionalized roles and collaboration mechanisms for non-state actors in civic education and participation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Objective: Undertake coordinated and integrated capacity building
rubrics_metrics.description: Undertake coordinated and integrated capacity building towards empowering responsible citizens and public institutions;
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Prioritizes training and capacity strengthening for both citizens and duty-bearers, coordinated across actors and levels.

rubrics_metrics.name: Objective: Promote effective participation in planning, budgeting and implementation
rubrics_metrics.description: Promote effective public participation in planning, budgeting and implementation of approved plans and budgets;
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Requires participation to be meaningfully integrated into planning and fiscal processes and not merely consultative.

rubrics_metrics.name: Objective: Promote effective participation of minorities and marginalized groups
rubrics_metrics.description: Promote effective participation of minorities and marginalized groups at all levels;
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Mandates targeted inclusion and measures to ensure special groups are meaningfully engaged.

rubrics_metrics.name: Objective: Guarantee adequate, secure and sustainable funding
rubrics_metrics.description: Guarantee adequate, secure and sustainable funding for public participation;
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Recognizes funding as a core enabler; implies budgeting, resourcing and financial planning for participation activities.

rubrics_metrics.name: Objective: Promote well-resourced, updated and implemented MEL systems
rubrics_metrics.description: Promote well-resourced, updated and effectively implemented monitoring, evaluation and learning systems for public participation;
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Calls for MEL frameworks, indicators, resourcing and dissemination of MEL outputs for accountability and learning.

rubrics_metrics.name: Objective: Promote responsive, functional and timely feedback and reporting mechanisms
rubrics_metrics.description: Promote responsive, functional and timely feedback and reporting mechanisms in order to build confidence in public participation process;
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Emphasizes closing the feedback loop—citizens must learn how their inputs were used and decisions justified.

rubrics_metrics.name: Objective: Promote effective handling of complaints
rubrics_metrics.description: Promote effective handling of complaints.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Requires accessible, publicised, and functioning complaints and redress pathways linked to participation processes.

rubrics_metrics.name: Guiding principle: Sovereignty of the people and equal opportunities for all
rubrics_metrics.description: Sovereignty of the people and equal opportunities for all
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Places citizens at the centre; participation must respect popular sovereignty and equality of opportunity.

rubrics_metrics.name: Guiding principle: Right to be involved in decision and policy making processes
rubrics_metrics.description: Right of every individual, group, community and organization to be involved in the decision and policy making processes
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Universal right to engage—applies across actors and levels.

rubrics_metrics.name: Guiding principle: Provision of adequate and effective mechanisms and opportunities for participation
rubrics_metrics.description: Provision of adequate and effective mechanisms and opportunities for participation for those interested in, or affected by decisions
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Obligation to create mechanisms that enable meaningful engagement for interested/affected parties.

rubrics_metrics.name: Guiding principle: Consultation between national and county governments and NSAs
rubrics_metrics.description: Consultation between the two levels of government in line with Article 6(2) of the Constitution and building relationships with Non State Actors
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Intergovernmental consultation and cooperation with NSAs are required.

rubrics_metrics.name: Guiding principle: Inclusion of minorities and marginalized groups
rubrics_metrics.description: Inclusion of minorities and the marginalized groups, including women, youth, elderly, PWDs and children
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Affirms affirmative measures to include identified vulnerable groups.

rubrics_metrics.name: Guiding principle: Non-discrimination and accommodation
rubrics_metrics.description: Non-discrimination and accommodation, respecting diversity, people’s values, culture, needs and customs
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Participation practices must be non-discriminatory and culturally sensitive.

rubrics_metrics.name: Guiding principle: Timely access to necessary information in accessible format
rubrics_metrics.description: Timely access to the necessary information in a language and form that is easy to comprehend, including accessible formats for People with Disabilities (PWDs) and through media that is accessible to the public
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Sets explicit accessibility standards for information dissemination.

rubrics_metrics.name: Guiding principle: Provision of civic education and capacity development
rubrics_metrics.description: Provision of civic education and the development of the necessary capacity for the public to effectively engage
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Requires investment in civic education as a precondition for meaningful participation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Guiding principle: Adherence to national values, Bill of Rights and fundamental freedoms
rubrics_metrics.description: National Values under Article 10, the Bill of Rights and Fundamental Freedoms in Chapter Four of the Constitution
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Participation must be exercised within constitutional values and rights.

rubrics_metrics.name: Guiding principle: Principles of leadership and integrity
rubrics_metrics.description: Principles of leadership and integrity in Chapter 6 of the Kenya Constitution
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Duty-bearers must observe leadership and integrity standards when conducting participation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Guiding principle: Provision of adequate funding for public participation
rubrics_metrics.description: Provision of adequate funding for public participation
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Financial resourcing is a guiding value and obligation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Guiding principle: Adequate monitoring, evaluation, learning and feedback mechanisms
rubrics_metrics.description: Adequate monitoring, evaluation, learning and feedback mechanisms
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Embedding MEL and feedback as core principles to sustain participation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Guiding principle: Adherence to devolution and separation of powers
rubrics_metrics.description: Adherence to the principles of devolution and separation of power
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Participation must respect constitutional governance structures and competencies.

rubrics_metrics.name: Guiding principle: Respect for child participation principles
rubrics_metrics.description: Respect for the principles of child participation, including child friendly environment, appropriate information, and non-intimidation
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Special protections and modalities when engaging children.

rubrics_metrics.name: Guiding principle: Access to remedial measures in cases of dispute
rubrics_metrics.description: Access to remedial measures in cases of dispute.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Participation frameworks must link to redress and dispute resolution options.

rubrics_metrics.name: Monitoring, Evaluation and Learning (MEL): Policy Objective
rubrics_metrics.description: The state will promote well-resourced updated and effectively implemented monitoring, evaluation and learning systems for public participation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: MEL is positioned to objectively track implementation, outputs and measure effectiveness; MEL outputs should be published and available for public consumption and learning.

rubrics_metrics.name: MEL: Policy Standards
rubrics_metrics.description: Governments at the two levels, in collaboration with other stakeholders will: (i) Put in place MEL systems and mechanisms for public participation in development projects and programmes; (ii) Integrate public participation within every MEL program in Government; (iii) Publish and disseminate annual reports with indicators on the status of public participation; (iv) Establish structured communication and feedback mechanisms to ensure that MEL initiatives are disseminated to the citizens and policy makers; and (v) Strengthen communities to actively participate in MEL, including auditing of public projects and programs.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Specifies concrete steps governments must take to operationalize MEL for participation, including integration, reporting, dissemination, and community involvement.

rubrics_metrics.name: Feedback and Reporting Mechanisms: Policy Objective
rubrics_metrics.description: The state will promote responsive, functional and timely feedback and reporting mechanisms in order to build confidence in public participation process.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Recognizes feedback as prerequisite for trust and continued citizen engagement.

rubrics_metrics.name: Feedback and Reporting Mechanisms: Policy Standards
rubrics_metrics.description: Governments at the two levels will: (i) Establish mechanisms for timely feedback and reporting on public participation at all levels; (ii) Review, formulate and implement plans on feedback on public participation; (iii) Ensure that responsible institutions develop guidelines on receiving and analysing feedback from citizens, sharing and incorporation into development processes; and (iv) Ensure reports provide justification for decisions made.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Requires institutionalising feedback processes, guidelines for handling inputs, and transparent justification of outcomes.

rubrics_metrics.name: Complaints and Redress Mechanisms: Policy Objective
rubrics_metrics.description: The state will promote effective handling of complaints.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Links participation to accessible redress mechanisms and constitutional rights to petition.

rubrics_metrics.name: Complaints and Redress Mechanisms: Policy Standards
rubrics_metrics.description: Governments at the two levels will collaborate with other stakeholders to: (i) Establish and strengthen complaints and redress mechanisms and procedures that are simple, available, publicised and understandable by users; (ii) Promote alternative dispute resolution mechanisms; (iii) Ensure internal complaints and redress mechanisms are established at all levels of government; (iv) Strengthen oversight institutions on complaints handling at national and county levels of government, particularly Commission on Administrative Justice; (v) Ensure compliance with existing laws and complaints reporting mechanisms; (vi) Sensitise citizens on complaints and redress mechanisms; and (vii) Provide for the development of a service delivery charter and ensure they are regularly reviewed and updated.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Sets out completeness of complaint handling system: accessibility, ADR, internal mechanisms, oversight strengthening, legal compliance, citizen sensitisation and service charters.

rubrics_metrics.name: Implementation principle: National orientation and language/accessibility requirement
rubrics_metrics.description: Public participation will take place at all levels including the lowest possible level of governance and will be conducted in English and Kiswahili in addition to other relevant languages commonly used in each specific locality. National and county Civic Education Units will ensure that public participation takes place in the most effective way inclusive of the lowest devolved units - village level.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Mandates multilingual approaches and engagement at the grassroots (village) level; identifies CCEUs as responsible units for effective local-level participation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Institutional framework: Coordinating Government Agency
rubrics_metrics.description: A multi-sectoral committee co-convened by the Office of the Attorney General and the Department of Justice and the Ministry of Devolution and ASAL will constitute the coordinating agency. The agency will include mandatory government bodies and NSAs relevant to the nine policy areas and will provide leadership and supervise coordination of policy implementation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Defines a central multi-sectoral coordinating mechanism to harmonize implementation across actors and levels.

rubrics_metrics.name: Role of MDAs and Constitutional Commissions and Independent Offices
rubrics_metrics.description: The role of Government Ministries, Departments and Agencies including Constitutional Commissions and Independent Offices will be to create an enabling environment for public participation to take place, including establishing the relevant department or office and appointing officers in charge of public participation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Requires institutional arrangements and designated officers within MDAs to operationalise participation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Role of County Governments
rubrics_metrics.description: The role of County Governments will be to promote principles of public participation as provided in the Constitution, the County Governments Act and in this policy. Within the public participation policy framework, Governments at the two levels will foster linkages with various development partners to provide financial, material and technical assistance as well as build capacity for sustainability.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Assigns county governments responsibilities for promotion, resourcing and partnership for participation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Role of Development Partners
rubrics_metrics.description: Development partners will play a complementary role towards realization of development of the goals and objectives of this policy. In particular, they will assist in leveraging resources and facilitating capacity building for public participation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Positions development partners as resource and capacity-building collaborators, not as primary implementers.

rubrics_metrics.name: Role of Non-State Actors (NSAs)
rubrics_metrics.description: The role of non-state actors will be to collaborate with Government to mobilize citizens and resources, disseminate the policy and participate in capacity building for both citizens and duty bearers. They will also collaborate with the government in public participation processes including civic education and mobilizing the citizens to participate in diverse aspects of public governance.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: NSAs are partners in mobilisation, civic education and capacity building; collaborative rather than adversarial relationship expected.

rubrics_metrics.name: Role of Citizens
rubrics_metrics.description: Citizens are the main pillars of the policy and have to actively be involved in the implementation of this policy including being actively engaged in monitoring, evaluation and learning. They have a duty to attend public participation meetings and to contribute effectively. Being the overall consumers of public participation, citizens are expected to exercise their sovereignty by holding duty bearers and all other agencies to account.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Citizens have responsibilities as well as rights—active engagement and holding duty-bearers accountable.

rubrics_metrics.name: Incorporation requirement: Public Participation Principles into SOPs
rubrics_metrics.description: Each Government at the two levels and related agencies must incorporate the principles of public participation and will establish a coordination unit and designate an officer in charge of coordination ensuring that public participation becomes part of each MDA, Constitutional Commissions and Independent Offices standard operating procedures.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Mandates institutionalisation via SOPs, coordination units and designated officers across agencies.

rubrics_metrics.name: Development of People’s Participation Charter (requirement)
rubrics_metrics.description: The two levels and related agencies will develop a People’s Participation Charter, which will set out the principles for participation, including specification of when and how the people of Kenya should participate as well as stipulating the opportunities available.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Charters are required instruments to make participation expectations explicit at each agency/level.

rubrics_metrics.name: Public Participation Guidelines and Annual Reporting requirement
rubrics_metrics.description: Each arm of government shall prepare guidelines on public participation indicating how they will engage with the public. Further, both National and County governments will make an Annual Public Participation Report detailing the level of public participation in each level of government and the challenges experienced. Each level of Government will outline in the Annual Report how they will be addressed in the next year and submit the same to the Coordinating Agency.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Requires agency-level guidance documents and annual reporting to the coordinating agency, including challenges and remedial plans.

rubrics_metrics.name: Legislative content to be addressed in guidelines/legislation
rubrics_metrics.description: Both the national and county governments will pass legislation to establish the relevant mechanisms and institutions to address the following issues: (i) Provide a working definition of public participation; (ii) How public participation will be conducted and the responsibilities of key stakeholders; (iii) Who should participate and how?; (iv) How each special interest group has been incorporated in the content of public participation; (v) Conditions for meaningful participation; (vi) Rights and duties of members of the public; (vii) Capacity building mechanisms for key stakeholders; and (viii) Timelines for participation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Specifies mandatory legislative/guideline content to ensure clarity on definitions, roles, inclusion, conditions, rights/duties, capacity building and timelines.

rubrics_metrics.name: M&E framework evaluation questions
rubrics_metrics.description: The monitoring and evaluation framework will address questions such as whether the participation exercise comprised a broadly representative sample of the population of the affected public; whether the issues of concern to the public, and relevant to the decision at hand, were taken into account in reaching a decision; whether timeliness, realistic milestones and deadlines were properly managed throughout the process; whether the involvement of the public was canvassed early enough; whether the public were able to participate in an effective forum; whether the public participation process provided the participants with the information, documents and data that they need to participate in an informed manner; whether the process for public participation sought out and facilitated the involvement of those potentially affected by or interested in a decision; whether the PLWDs were effectively engaged; and whether public participation process gave a feedback to participants how their input informed decisions made.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provides concrete evaluative criteria for assessing the quality and meaningfulness of a participation exercise; these questions form the backbone of performance measurement.

rubrics_metrics.name: Policy review cycle
rubrics_metrics.description: The Kenya Policy on Public Participation will be reviewed every five years in line with the current and future needs of Kenya.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Mandates periodic policy review to ensure relevance and responsiveness.
